plan: With 3 bidders and uniform value distribution on [0,49], the standard first-price auction Nash equilibrium strategy is to bid (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for 3 bidders. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $31, so optimal bid ≈ $20.67. This shades my bid appropriately below value to maximize expected profit while maintaining competitive winning chances against Betty and Charles.

This is effectively a second-price auction: I pay the highest bid among others if I win, not my own bid. In second-price auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value, since bidding higher risks overpaying above my value, and bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. My value is $6, so I will bid exactly that to maximize expected profit.

My private value for this item is $0. Since winning at any positive price would result in a loss (paying more than the item is worth to me), the only rational bid is $0. This ensures I cannot lose money - if I win at $0, I break even, and if I don't win, I also break even. Bidding anything above $0 risks negative profit if I win.
